answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to anchor a verifiable work history in a public atlas of attestations, like a ship's log across an ocean of transactions. New identities start with near-zero trust and earn reputation only through repeated, costly, peer-verified work. A sudden gale of fresh accounts cannot fake that history, because attestations are chained, timestamped, and tied to prior useful output, so creating many fake identities costs far more than any reward they could extract.
